authors: Sapkota, R.; Roumeliotis, K. I.; Karkee, M.
title: AI agents vs. agentic AI: A conceptual taxonomy, applications and challenges
verification: [V-open: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10468, accessed 2026-11-14] abstract; published metadata from academic_register AG01 (Crossref)
method_and_data: Conceptual review with search strategy; application mapping
key_findings: Separates AI agents (modular, LLM-driven, task-specific, tool-using) from agentic AI (multi-agent collaboration, dynamic task decomposition, persistent memory, coordinated autonomy); positions generative AI as the precursor.
key_quote_with_page: "Generative AI is positioned as a precursor providing the foundation, with AI agents advancing through tool integration, prompt engineering, and reasoning enhancements." (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports: generative phase precedes agentic phase; adds a three-step ladder (GenAI, AI agent, agentic AI)
notes: Already AG01 in academic_register. Cite 2026 (arXiv 2025). Technical not business lens; the thesis can use the ladder but should note the vendor use of 'agent' is looser (Gartner agent washing, AG046).

authors: Abou Ali, M.; Dornaika, F.; Charafeddine, J.
title: Agentic AI: A comprehensive survey of architectures, applications, and future directions
verification: [V-open: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.25445, accessed 2026-11-14] abstract (arXiv v1 lists two authors); journal metadata from academic_register AG02
key_findings: Dual-paradigm framework: symbolic/classical agents (algorithmic planning, persistent state) vs neural/generative agents (stochastic generation, prompt-driven orchestration); warns of 'conceptual retrofitting'; paradigm choice is strategic (symbolic in safety-critical domains).
key_quote_with_page: "often conflating modern neural systems with outdated symbolic models -- a practice known as conceptual retrofitting" (abstract, arXiv v1)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: neutral: cautions against equating LLM agents with classical agent theory
notes: Already AG02 in academic_register. Useful for the definitions section: today's SaaS 'agents' are the neural/generative lineage.

authors: Kumar, N.; Wei, X.; Zhang, H.
title: Agentic artificial intelligence as a new frontier in information systems: Promise, peril, and research opportunities
verification: [V-meta: Crossref 2026-11-14] no abstract available (ScienceDirect blocked; Crossref record has none)
key_findings: Content not verified. Title frames agentic AI as an IS frontier with promise, peril and research opportunities.
key_quote_with_page: not read

title: The role of agentic AI in shaping a smart future: A systematic review
key_findings: Content not verified; metadata only.

authors: Wooldridge, M.; Jennings, N. R.
title: Intelligent agents: theory and practice
method_and_data: Review of agent theory, architectures and languages

theory_or_lens: Classical agent theory (weak and strong notions of agency)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: neutral: foundational definition
notes: Classic foundation; the weak notion (autonomy, social ability, reactivity, pro-activeness) is the one that matches LLM agents. Pages beyond the abstract not read; the four properties are [M].

title: Artificial intelligence: A modern approach (4th ed.)

key_quote_with_page: not read

authors: Wang, L.; Ma, C.; Feng, X.; et al.
title: A survey on large language model based autonomous agents
venue_or_publisher: Frontiers of Computer Science 18 (article number to be checked)

key_quote_with_page: "This has sparked an upsurge in studies investigating LLM-based autonomous agents." (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: neutral: definitional

authors: Xi, Z.; Chen, W.; Guo, X.; et al.
title: The rise and potential of large language model based agents: A survey
verification: [V-open: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.07864, accessed 2026-11-14]; journal metadata via Crossref 2026-11-14
key_findings: Proposes a general framework (brain, perception, action) for LLM agents and discusses single-agent, multi-agent and human-agent cooperation scenarios.
key_quote_with_page: "AI agents are artificial entities that sense their environment, make decisions, and take actions." (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: neutral: definitional

authors: Feng, K. J. K.; McDonald, D. W.; Zhang, A. X.
title: Levels of autonomy for AI agents
venue_or_publisher: arXiv:2506.12469 (also Knight First Amendment Institute essay series)
key_findings: Five levels of agent autonomy defined by the role the user takes (operator, collaborator, consultant, approver, observer); autonomy is a design decision separate from capability and environment; proposes 'autonomy certificates' for governance.
key_quote_with_page: "We argue that an agent's level of autonomy can be treated as a deliberate design decision, separate from its capability and operational environment." (abstract)
theory_or_lens: Human-agent interaction; levels of automation (extends Parasuraman et al. 2000)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports: autonomy is a product choice, which is how vendors set 'agency' levels
notes: Gives a ready scale for the agency coding used in the case files (agency 1 to 3). Preprint; peer-review status not confirmed.

authors: Mitchell, M.; Ghosh, A.; Luccioni, A. S.; Pistilli, G.
title: Fully autonomous AI agents should not be developed
method_and_data: Position paper drawing on literature and product marketing to delineate agent levels
key_findings: Risks to people increase with the autonomy of a system; documents value trade-offs at each level.
key_quote_with_page: "The more control a user cedes to an AI agent, the more risks to people arise." (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: challenges: full autonomy as the endpoint of the agentic phase
notes: Normative, not about business models. Use as support for governance as a lever (rival hypothesis) and for why vendors keep humans as approvers.

authors: Baird, A.; Maruping, L. M.
title: The next generation of research on IS use: A theoretical framework of delegation to and from agentic IS artifacts
key_findings: IS use theory assumes human agency primacy; agentic IS artifacts can initiate action and accept responsibility for tasks with ambiguous requirements; introduces delegation as a foundation for a new generation of IS use research.
key_quote_with_page: "Agentic IS artifacts are no longer passive tools waiting to be used, are no longer always subordinate to the human agent" (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports: the user-tool relation changes from use to delegation
notes: Top-journal IS anchor that predates LLM agents; the thesis can ground 'agents as users of software' on it. Pre-LLM, so say so.

authors: Berente, N.; Gu, B.; Recker, J.; Santhanam, R.
title: Managing artificial intelligence
key_findings: Managing AI concerns three interdependent facets: autonomy, learning, inscrutability.
key_quote_with_page: "making decisions about three related, interdependent facets of AI: autonomy, learning, and inscrutability" (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports: autonomy is a managerial variable
notes: Peripheral. Use for the autonomy dimension only.

authors: Raisch, S.; Krakowski, S.
title: Artificial intelligence and management: The automation-augmentation paradox
key_findings: Content not verified; title states that automation and augmentation form a paradox, i.e. they are interdependent. [M] for the argument.
key_quote_with_page: not read
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: neutral: unverified
notes: Relevant to the generative (augmentation) versus agentic (automation) contrast. Read before using.

authors: Kolt, N.
title: Governing AI agents
method_and_data: Legal and economic analysis (principal-agent theory, agency law)
key_findings: Field moves from generative models to agents that plan and execute; agency problems of information asymmetry, discretionary authority and loyalty; conventional incentive, monitoring and enforcement may fail for uninterpretable, fast agents.
key_quote_with_page: "a fundamental transition from generative models that can produce synthetic content to artificial agents that can plan and execute complex tasks with only limited human involvement" (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports: explicit generative to agentic transition; supports governance angle
notes: The principal-agent frame is also the frame used against outcome-based pricing (the vendor as agent of the buyer). Publication venue to be checked.

authors: Yao, S.; Zhao, J.; Yu, D.; et al.
title: ReAct: Synergizing reasoning and acting in language models
method_and_data: Prompting method evaluated on QA, fact verification and interactive decision benchmarks
key_findings: Interleaves reasoning traces and actions so models can use external sources (APIs) and update plans; foundation of the tool-using agent loop.
key_quote_with_page: "allowing for greater synergy between the two: reasoning traces help the model induce, track, and update action plans" (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: neutral: technical foundation of tool use
notes: Cite only for the technical origin of the agent loop; the venue (ICLR 2023) is from memory.

authors: Yang, J.; Jimenez, C. E.; Wettig, A.; et al.
title: SWE-agent: Agent-computer interfaces enable automated software engineering
key_findings: Posits LM agents as 'a new category of end users' that need purpose-built interfaces; a custom agent-computer interface raises performance sharply (pass@1 12.5% on SWE-bench at the time).
key_quote_with_page: "we posit that LM agents represent a new category of end users with their own needs and abilities, and would benefit from specially-built interfaces to the software they use" (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports: interface design for agents matters (precursor of AX)
notes: Earliest academic statement I found that agents are users with their own interface needs. Evidence that how a product is exposed changes what agents can do with it.

authors: Lù, X. H.; Kamath, G.; Mosbach, M.; Reddy, S.
title: Build the web for agents, not agents for the web
key_findings: Argues for an Agentic Web Interface (AWI) optimised for agent capabilities rather than forcing agents through human-designed interfaces, and distinguishes AWI from API-based bypass.
key_quote_with_page: "rather than forcing web agents to adapt to interfaces designed for humans, we should develop a new interaction paradigm specifically optimized for agentic capabilities" (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports: disintermediation of the GUI, dual interfaces
notes: Academic counterpart to AX. Position paper, no evidence on adoption.

authors: Yang, Y.; Ma, M.; Huang, Y.; et al.
title: Agentic Web: Weaving the next web with AI agents
key_findings: Describes a shift from human-driven to machine-to-machine interaction in which intent is delegated; a three-dimension model (intelligence, interaction, economics).
key_quote_with_page: "This transition from human-driven to machine-to-machine interaction allows intent to be delegated" (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports: machine-to-machine interaction as the next phase
notes: Broad and partly technical; cite for the 'agentic web' label.

authors: Rothschild, D. M.; Mobius, M.; Hofman, J. M.; et al.
title: The agentic economy
key_findings: Early generative gains are confined to predefined tasks inside existing workflows; the larger impact lies in reducing communication frictions between consumers and businesses via assistant agents and service agents; distinguishes unscripted from unrestricted interactions; discusses walled gardens versus an open web of agents.
key_quote_with_page: "the more profound economic impact lies in reducing communication frictions between consumers and businesses" (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports: separates a generative phase (productivity inside workflows) from an agentic phase (market reorganisation)
notes: Strongest source for the thesis's generative/agentic split in economic terms. Authors are Microsoft researchers (a platform with an interest).

authors: Shahidi, P.; Rusak, G.; Manning, B. S.; Fradkin, A.; Horton, J. J.
title: The Coasean singularity? Demand, supply, and market design with AI agents
venue_or_publisher: NBER Working Paper 34468; chapter in The Economics of Transformative AI
key_findings: Agents lower search, communication and contracting costs but create congestion and price obfuscation; on the supply side firms design, integrate and monetise agents, with outcomes hinging on whether agents operate within or across platforms; net welfare is an empirical question.
key_quote_with_page: "On the supply side, firms will design, integrate, and monetize agents, with outcomes hinging on whether agents operate within or across platforms." (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: mixed: efficiency gains but new frictions
notes: Fradkin is employed by Amazon (disclosed). The within-versus-across-platform question is exactly the S1 versus S2 choice.

authors: Tomasev, N.; Franklin, M.; Leibo, J. Z.; Jacobs, J.; Cunningham, W. A.; Gabriel, I.; Osindero, S.
title: Virtual agent economies
key_findings: A new economic layer where agents transact beyond direct human oversight; permeable versus impermeable, emergent versus intentional; calls for steerable agent markets (auctions, mission economies, trust infrastructure).
key_quote_with_page: "a new economic layer where agents transact and coordinate at scales and speeds beyond direct human oversight" (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: neutral: speculative macro framing
notes: Macro and speculative. Use sparingly.

authors: Bansal, G.; Hua, W.; Huang, Z.; et al.
title: Magentic Marketplace: An open-source environment for studying agentic markets
method_and_data: Simulation of two-sided agentic marketplaces (assistant agents and service agents)
key_findings: Frontier models approach optimal welfare only under ideal search; performance degrades with scale; severe first-proposal bias gives 10-30x advantages for response speed over quality; agents are vulnerable to manipulation.
key_quote_with_page: "all models exhibit severe first-proposal bias, creating 10-30x advantages for response speed over quality" (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: challenges: agent-mediated markets are not yet reliable choosers
notes: Companion to Cherep et al. (NEW14 in academic_register). Implication: being callable and fast may matter more than being best, which is a design target for AX.

authors: Pattison, C.; Boulos, M.; Kolt, N.; Li, C.; Piccardi, T.; Lazar, S.
title: The agentic web requires new normative infrastructure
key_findings: Online platforms can block and degrade agent access, often in secret, under outdated laws and terms of service; few distinctions are drawn between malicious bots and agents acting under delegated authority; argues for norms governing agentic access.
key_quote_with_page: "allow online platforms to block and degrade agent access, often in secret" (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports: access terms are a strategic and normative variable
notes: Directly relevant to SQ1 (access terms). Read together with AG073 (Amazon v Perplexity) and AG072 (Slack API terms).

authors: Hydari, M. Z.; Muzaffar, F.
title: Going headless? On the boundaries of vertical AI firms
key_findings: General-purpose agents unbundle workflow, domain logic and accountability; 'going headless' (cede interface, expose expertise as callable services) is right for some firms and destructive for others, who cede value capture through architectural choices that look like interface decisions.
key_quote_with_page: "going headless is correct for some firms and destructive for others, and that the latter often cede their value capture inadvertently through architectural choices that look like interface decisions" (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: mixed: headless is conditional
notes: Already NEW02. Covers vertical AI firms, not creation SaaS; the gap is whether the boundary logic carries over to artifact-editing tools. Salesforce Headless 360 (AG042) is the incumbent counterpart.

authors: Hydari, M. Z.; Muzaffar, F.
title: Redrawing the AI map: A theory of accountability boundaries in agentic ecosystems
key_findings: Agentic orchestrators lower interface and assembly costs, but capabilities whose outputs require evidence, review, signoff or assignable responsibility may stay integrated; introduces 'accountability assets'.
key_quote_with_page: "AI-enabled capabilities whose outputs require evidence, review, signoff, or assignable responsibility may retain integrated accountability boundaries even when their technical interfaces become modular" (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports: governance and accountability as defence
notes: Already NEW03. Fits Grammarly's authorship/AI-detection logic; weaker fit for Canva and Figma where output accountability is lower.

authors: Klotz, D.
title: The buy-or-build decision, revisited: How agentic AI changes the economics of enterprise software
method_and_data: Conceptual (transaction cost economics plus resource-based view)
key_findings: Agentic coding reshapes make-or-buy determinants; re-evaluates the 'SaaSocalypse' narrative and offers a typology of enterprise applications by sensitivity.
key_quote_with_page: "The 'SaaSocalypse' narrative predicts that AI will render large segments of the Software-as-a-Service market obsolete by enabling firms to build software in-house at a fraction of historical cost." (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: challenges: the strong SaaSpocalypse claim (conditional on application type)
notes: Already NEW04. Targets enterprise applications, not creation tools for non-technical users; extension to prosumer creation SaaS is open.

authors: Bohnsack, R.; de Wet, M.
title: AI is the strategy: From agentic AI to autonomous business models onto strategy in the age of AI
venue_or_publisher: arXiv:2506.17339 (under review at Strategy Science per arXiv)
method_and_data: Concept paper with two illustrative cases (getswan.ai; hypothetical Ryanair)
key_findings: Agentic AI can execute core mechanisms of value creation, delivery and capture; defines Autonomous Business Models; 'AI as the strategy itself'; new competition between AI-led firms.
key_quote_with_page: "agentic AI ... can increasingly execute the core mechanisms of value creation, delivery, and capture. This shift reframes AI not as a tool to support strategy, but as the strategy itself." (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports: agentic phase changes the business model itself, not just features
notes: Already AI11. Illustrative cases only (one start-up, one hypothetical). Gamma is the closest real analogue.

authors: Najmaei, A.; Sadeghinejad, Z.
title: From instrument to economic actor: Generative and agentic AI as a new logic of business model innovation
method_and_data: Concept paper integrating business model, activity system and dynamic capability research
key_findings: Three logics of AI-enabled BMI: supporting (instrument), generative (co-creator), agentic (delegated economic actor).
key_quote_with_page: "a supporting logic (AI as instrument), a generative logic (AI as co-creator), and an agentic log[ic]" (abstract, truncated in my read)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports: distinct generative and agentic logics
notes: Already AI09. The only source I found that separates generative from agentic logic in BMI terms; mid-tier outlet (MDPI). Full text not read beyond abstract.

authors: Prole, J.; Prole, H.
title: Modular execution, sticky accountability firm: Scope and value capture under agentic AI
key_findings: Agentic AI increases productive modularity faster than accountability modularity: execution can be externalised while responsibility stays with the focal firm; 'boundary decoupling'; accountable-scale capability.
key_quote_with_page: "Execution can be decomposed and externalized, while responsibility for consequential work may remain attached to the focal firm." (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports: governance as a lever
notes: SSRN working paper, new and unreviewed. Complements AG025.

authors: Gerlach, S.
title: The organizational role of AI agents and agentic AI in the firm: Toward a theory of smart systems
method_and_data: Conceptual theory (information-processing theory, cybernetics, decision rights)
key_findings: Agentic AI moves AI from information provision to planning, decision-making, tool use and action; distinguishes self-regulation from delegated autonomy within organisationally bounded Smart Systems.
key_quote_with_page: "Agentic AI expands the organizational role of artificial intelligence from information provision toward planning, decision-making, tool use, action, and feedback." (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: neutral: definitional
notes: SSRN working paper. Possibly useful for the generative-to-agentic definition (information versus action).

authors: Guimaraes Figueira, M.
title: Brand erasure: A research agenda for brand theory in agentic AI markets
key_findings: AI assistants become the dominant intermediary; the brand can be omitted, paraphrased or substituted at the moment of action; 'brand erasure' distinct from dilution and disintermediation.
key_quote_with_page: "the brand can be omitted from the answer, paraphrased into the synthesis, or substituted at the moment of action without the consumer ever noticing" (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports: disintermediation of the product by agents
notes: Consumer-brand context; transfers to SaaS as 'product erasure' when an agent hides which tool it called. Working paper.

authors: Hou, X.; Zhao, Y.; Wang, S.; Wang, H.
title: Model Context Protocol (MCP): Landscape, security threats, and future research directions
method_and_data: Systematic study of the MCP server lifecycle (creation, deployment, operation, maintenance; 16 activities) and a threat taxonomy
key_findings: MCP defined as an open standard for bi-directional communication and dynamic discovery between models and tools; lifecycle risk analysis and threat taxonomy.
key_quote_with_page: "an emerging open standard that defines a unified, bi-directional communication and dynamic discovery protocol between AI models and external tools or resources" (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: neutral: security risks of S2
notes: Technical. Use for the claim that opening a product through MCP creates security and governance exposure.

authors: Hasan, M. M.; Li, H.; Fallahzadeh, E.; Rajbahadur, G. K.; Adams, B.; Hassan, A. E.
title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) at first glance: Studying the security and maintainability of MCP servers
method_and_data: Static and MCP-specific analysis of 1,899 open-source MCP servers
key_findings: 7.2% of servers contain general vulnerabilities and 5.5% exhibit MCP-specific tool poisoning; eight distinct vulnerability types, only three overlapping traditional ones.
key_quote_with_page: "7.2% of servers contain general vulnerabilities, and 5.5% exhibit MCP-specific tool poisoning" (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: challenges: S2 is not risk-free
notes: Open-source servers, not vendor-run official servers. Qualify when applying to SaaS vendors.

authors: Guo, H.; Hao, Y.; Zhang, Y.; Xu, M.; Lv, P.; Chen, J.; Cheng, X.
title: A measurement study of Model Context Protocol ecosystem
method_and_data: Crawl of six MCP marketplaces: 17,630 raw entries, 8,401 valid projects (8,060 servers, 341 clients), 14 days
key_findings: More than half of listed projects are invalid or low-value; dependency monocultures and uneven maintenance; clients in a transitional phase of protocol and connection patterns.
key_quote_with_page: "more than half of listed projects are invalid or low-value" (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: challenges: headline server counts overstate real adoption
notes: Best available empirical check on MCP adoption hype; contrast with the '10,000+ active public servers' claim in AG039. Snapshot of Sept 2025.

authors: Ehtesham, A.; Singh, A.; Gupta, G. K.; Kumar, S.
title: A survey of agent interoperability protocols: MCP, ACP, A2A and ANP
key_findings: Compares MCP (tool access), ACP, A2A (agent-to-agent delegation) and ANP (open-network discovery) across interaction modes, discovery and security; proposes phased adoption.
key_quote_with_page: "Ad-hoc integrations are difficult to scale, secure, and generalize across domains." (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: neutral: descriptive
notes: Descriptive; no strategic analysis of who gains from each protocol. Gap for the thesis: vendor strategy around protocols is undocumented academically.

authors: Anthropic
title: Introducing the Model Context Protocol
key_findings: MCP open-sourced as a standard for connecting AI assistants to the systems where data lives; specification, SDKs, local server support in Claude Desktop, and reference servers (Google Drive, Slack, GitHub, Postgres). Early adopters Block and Apollo.
key_quote_with_page: "Every new data source requires its own custom implementation, making truly connected systems difficult to scale." (web page, n/p)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: neutral: primary document, interested party
notes: Anthropic is also a competitor to the focal firms (Claude Design, Cowork). Date 25 Nov 2024 from the search listing; page body does not show it in my extract.

authors: Surapaneni, R.; Jha, M.; Vakoc, M.; Segal, T. (Google)
title: Announcing the Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A)
key_findings: Open protocol for agent-to-agent collaboration across vendors, 50+ launch partners (Atlassian, Box, Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow, Workday, large consultancies); positioned as complementing MCP.
key_quote_with_page: "A2A is an open protocol that complements Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP), which provides helpful tools and context to agents." (web page, n/p)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: neutral: primary document

authors: The Linux Foundation
title: Linux Foundation announces the formation of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) with MCP, goose and AGENTS.md
key_findings: MCP moves into a neutral foundation with founding contributions from Anthropic, Block and OpenAI; platinum members include AWS, Google, Microsoft, Cloudflare, Bloomberg.
key_quote_with_page: "MCP is the universal standard protocol for connecting AI models to tools, data and applications" (web page, n/p)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports: MCP is becoming neutral infrastructure
notes: Self-description by the foundation. Neutral governance lowers lock-in risk for vendors adopting S2.

authors: Anthropic
title: Donating the Model Context Protocol and establishing the Agentic AI Foundation
key_findings: Claims more than 10,000 active public MCP servers, adoption by ChatGPT, Cursor, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot and VS Code, 97M+ monthly SDK downloads, a connector directory with 75+ connectors, an official registry.
key_quote_with_page: "There are now more than 10,000 active public MCP servers, covering everything from developer tools to Fortune 500 deployments" (web page, n/p)

key_findings: Agentic Commerce Protocol and Shared Payment Token let ChatGPT initiate purchases without exposing buyer credentials; orders flow to the merchant backend, which remains seller of record.

title: Introducing Salesforce Headless 360: no browser required

key_quote_with_page: "If your platform requires humans to click through UIs or write code directly to make progress, it is not ready for the Agentic Enterprise." (web page, n/p)

authors: Biilmann, M.
title: Introducing AX: Why agent experience matters
